events.title: Telegram
events.text:
A top Hamas commander who held Israeli hostage Omer Shem Tov in captivity was killed in a strike in Gaza City earlier this week, the military and Shin Bet announce.
The strike on Sunday killed Jamal Abu Saeed, who the IDF says served as chief of operations in Hamas's military intelligence.
"During the war, Abu Saeed held Omer Shem Tov captive in Hamas captivity," the joint statement says.
Abu Saeed held other senior roles in Hamas over the years, including overseeing the training of Hamas operatives outside the Gaza Strip, serving as an anti-tank battalion commander, and being "responsible for military specialization in Hamas' Central Brigade," the military says.
Abu Saeed was also "responsible for Hamas's relations with various countries" and he "served as a significant source of knowledge for the terror organization," the IDF says.
The IDF says that recently, Abu Saeed had been advancing attacks on troops and Israeli civilians and acted to restore Hamas's capabilities, "in systematic violation of the ceasefire."

Lebanon's health ministry confirms that one person was killed and another was wounded in an Israeli drone strike on a motorcycle in the town of Qabrikha in the country's south this afternoon.
The slain man is identified in reports as Muhammad Nasser Yousef, a paramedic with the Hezbollah-allied Amal movement's Risala Scouts.
The IDF has not yet commented on the strike, the first in Lebanon in weeks.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Six Palestinian terror operatives were killed in Israeli strikes in the Gaza Strip earlier this week, the military and Shin Bet announce.
The IDF says separate strikes on Monday in southern Gaza's Khan Younis killed Mahmoud Jihad Mohammad Qafa, a commander of a Hamas sniper cell, and Asaad Suleiman Salman Qashta, a member of the Army of Islam faction who "facilitated smuggling into the Gaza Strip."
In another strike on Sunday in Khan Younis, four members of Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad were killed.
They are identified by the IDF and Shin Bet as Mohammad Zakaria Al-Jamal, a Hamas cell commander; Mohammad Amin Al-Namas, a Hamas operative; Shaher Mohammad Zaarab, commander of a company in Hamas's elite Nukhba Force; and Mohammad Ali Abu Shaar, an Islamic Jihad sniper operative.
The IDF says all of the operatives had recently been advancing attacks on troops and Israeli civilians and acted to restore the capabilities of the terror groups, "in systematic violation of the ceasefire."

🇺🇸🇮🇷US Treasury issues new Iran-linked sanctions, continuing escalatory actions
Individuals and companies in India and Turkey have been hit with US economic sanctions as part of President Donald Trump’s “Operation Economic Outcast” for allegedly aiding Iran, just a day after Democrats’ victory in the midterm elections.
💬 “We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime, whether by land, sea, or air,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.
Suniel Kumar Sharma, his wife Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, and two other Indian citizens allegedly defrauded maritime regulatory authorities in several countries, including Guyana, Eswatini and Laos, by claiming to represent them and issuing flags and certifications. This allowed vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies to evade international restrictions and continue operating, according to the US Treasury.
The department also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc. for its support of Iran’s aviation sector.

events.text:
🇺🇸Trump says Iran war will end whenever he wants, brushes off impeachment fears
US President Donald Trump acknowledged that the war with Iran may have contributed to Republicans' midterm defeat by temporarily driving up gasoline prices, but insisted he would make the same decision again.
🔊"If I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again," Trump said, arguing that Iran must never acquire nuclear weapons.
Asked when the war would end, he replied: "Whenever I wanted to."
Trump also dismissed concerns about possible impeachment by the new Democratic-controlled Congress.
🔊"Not even a little bit," he said, arguing that an impeachment attempt would "destroy the Democrat Party."
Trump added that he was open to working with Democrats, provided they did not seek to obstruct his agenda.
